author.writingStory: Began writing in fourth grade with a Thanksgiving poem the class loved; spent years writing skits, poems and cards for loved ones. Wrote Book One while in school and working full time on third shift, and planned to tuck it in her closet; her siblings were excited, and her publisher asked for a cliffhanger, which grew the book into a three-part series. (From her own document, 2026-11-22.)

coverSymbols: The Lord spoke to Laketha about the lotus flower, which grows in muddy water and blooms above the surface: rebirth, resilience and spiritual awakening. She kept it in mind as she designed the cover.
Tamela is not defined by physical features but by a flower in bloom, rising from the murky water so every woman can see herself in her.
Yellow was her mother’s favourite colour, so the flower pays homage to her.
Everything that held Tamela bound: pain, regret, unforgiveness, doubt, lack of faith and unhealthy relationships.
Transformation and rebirth: the emotional and spiritual metamorphosis that comes before we emerge into the beauty the world sees.

readingCircleQuestions: What does "redemption" mean to you, and did the book change that definition?
On the first cover, briars hold her bound: pain, regret, unforgiveness, doubt. Which of these do women carry most quietly, and why do they go unspoken?
Why does change so often arrive as a process rather than an event? Where have you seen that in your own life?
What sustains belief when circumstances give it nothing to stand on?
Blooming with work still to do
On the second cover she is in full bloom, yet some vines still hold her. What does it look like to flourish while there is still work to be done?
What is one practice, daily, unglamorous, faithful, that helps a person live out a new chapter?

items: Where can I buy Laketha's books?
Both books are on Amazon in paperback and Kindle. Signed copies are available by request; write to hello@lakethahicks.com.
Which book should I read first?
Start with Redemption: The Story of a Woman (2020), then Redemptions Journey (2022). Either stands alone, but together they trace the full arc from breaking to blooming.
Are the books a series?
Yes. What Laketha thought would be one book became the three-part Redemption series. Book One (2020) and Book Two (2022) are available now.
Who publishes her books?
Write by Faith Publications.
Can our book club or group read them together?
Please do. Discussion questions are free on the books page, and Laketha welcomes invitations to visit reading circles.
How can I contact Laketha about her books?
Use the contact page or write to hello@lakethahicks.com.
